answer:
**RE-LY (dabigatran 110 mg and 150 mg vs warfarin):** major bleeding 3.36%/yr with warfarin vs 2.71%/yr with 110 mg (P=0.003) and 3.11%/yr with 150 mg (P=0.31) — reduced at the lower dose, not significantly different at 150 mg. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P=0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.31)."} -->

**ROCKET AF (rivaroxaban vs warfarin):** no significant difference in major bleeding, but intracranial hemorrhage (0.5% vs 0.7%, P=0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs 0.5%, P=0.003) were less frequent with rivaroxaban. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"There was no significant between-group difference in the risk of major bleeding, although intracranial and fatal bleeding occurred less frequently in the rivaroxaban group."} --> Major or nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding was 14.9%/yr vs 14.5%/yr (HR 1.03; 95% CI 0.96–1.11; P=0.44). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1475 patients in the rivaroxaban group (14.9% per year) and in 1449 in the warfarin group (14.5% per year) (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P=0.44)"} -->

**ARISTOTLE (apixaban vs warfarin):** major bleeding 2.13%/yr vs 3.09%/yr (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60–0.80; P<0.001) — significantly lower with apixaban. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 2.13% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 3.09% per year in the warfarin group (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.80; P<0.001)"} -->

**ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban 60 mg high-dose and 30 mg low-dose vs warfarin):** annualized major bleeding 3.43% with warfarin vs 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.71–0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001) — both doses significantly lower than warfarin. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"The annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.43% with warfarin versus 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)."} -->

So: significantly less major bleeding than warfarin for apixaban and both edoxaban doses, less at dabigatran 110 mg only, and no significant difference for rivaroxaban or dabigatran 150 mg (though rivaroxaban reduced intracranial and fatal bleeding). Note the four trials used somewhat different definitions/reporting of major bleeding, so the rates are not strictly head-to-head comparable.

- **RE-LY (dabigatran 150 mg):** lower rates of stroke and systemic embolism than warfarin; the 110 mg dose gave rates similar to warfarin. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"Dabigatran administered at a dose of 150 mg, as compared with warfarin, was associated with lower rates of stroke and systemic embolism but similar rates of major hemorrhage." --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"dabigatran given at a dose of 110 mg was associated with rates of stroke and systemic embolism that were similar to those associated with warfarin"} -->

Major bleeding (annualized rates) versus warfarin in the four pivotal trials:

- **RE-LY (dabigatran 150 mg BID):** 3.11%/yr vs 3.36%/yr with warfarin (P=0.31 — not significantly different); dabigatran 110 mg BID was lower at 2.71%/yr (P=0.003). The paper concludes 150 mg gave "similar rates of major hemorrhage" to warfarin, while 110 mg gave lower rates. (Dabigatran versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P=0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.31)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"Dabigatran administered at a dose of 150 mg, as compared with warfarin, was associated with lower rates of stroke and systemic embolism but similar rates of major hemorrhage."} -->

- **ROCKET AF (rivaroxaban 20 mg daily):** no significant between-group difference in major bleeding, though intracranial and fatal bleeding occurred less often with rivaroxaban. (Rivaroxaban versus warfarin in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"There was no significant between-group difference in the risk of major bleeding, although intracranial and fatal bleeding occurred less frequently in the rivaroxaban group."} -->
Note: the knowledge base does not give the numeric major-bleeding rates for ROCKET AF itself (the figures 18.04% vs 16.42%/yr belong to J-ROCKET AF, a separate Japanese trial).

- **ARISTOTLE (apixaban 5 mg BID):** 2.13%/yr vs 3.09%/yr with warfarin (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60–0.80; P<0.001) — significantly less major bleeding. (Apixaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 2.13% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 3.09% per year in the warfarin group (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.80; P<0.001)"} -->

- **ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban):** 3.43%/yr with warfarin vs 2.75%/yr with high-dose edoxaban (60 mg; HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.71–0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61%/yr with low-dose edoxaban (30 mg; HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001) — both doses significantly lower. (Edoxaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"The annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.43% with warfarin versus 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)."} -->

So: significantly less major bleeding with apixaban and both edoxaban regimens, no significant difference with rivaroxaban or dabigatran 150 mg, and less bleeding with dabigatran 110 mg.

answer:
**ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban vs warfarin, median TTR 68.4%)** — low-dose (30 mg) edoxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke/systemic embolism, but with no efficacy advantage and a strong reduction in major bleeding. During treatment, the annualized primary event rate was 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% with warfarin (HR 1.07; 97.5% CI 0.87–1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority), and in the intention-to-treat analysis there was an unfavorable trend (HR 1.13; 97.5% CI 0.96–1.34; P=0.10). Major bleeding was 1.61% vs 3.43% (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001). Both regimens were noninferior with significantly lower bleeding and cardiovascular death.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 1.07; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 0.87 to 1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and an unfavorable trend with low-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 1.13; 97.5% CI, 0.96 to 1.34; P=0.10)" -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)."} -->

**Meta-analysis of the four pivotal trials (RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48; 71,683 participants)** — pooled low-dose NOAC regimens gave stroke/systemic embolic event reductions similar to warfarin (RR 1.03; 0.84–1.27; p=0.74) and a more favorable bleeding profile (0.65; 0.43–1.00; p=0.05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1.28; 1.02–1.60; p=0.045). Separately, the relative reduction in major bleeding was greater where centre-based TTR was <66% than ≥66% (0.69, 0.59–0.81 vs 0.93, 0.76–1.13; p for interaction 0.022).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"Low-dose new oral anticoagulant regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (1·03, 0·84-1·27; p=0·74), and a more favourable bleeding profile (0·65, 0·43-1·00; p=0·05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1·28, 1·02-1·60; p=0·045)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"there was a greater relative reduction in major bleeding with new oral anticoagulants when the centre-based time in therapeutic range was less than 66% than when it was 66% or more (0·69, 0·59-0·81 vs 0·93, 0·76-1·13; p for interaction 0·022)"} -->

**ELDERCARE-AF (15 mg edoxaban vs placebo)** — in Japanese patients ≥80 years with nonvalvular AF judged unsuitable for approved-dose anticoagulation (984 randomized, 492 per arm), edoxaban was superior to placebo for stroke/systemic embolism: annualized 2.3% vs 6.7% (HR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19–0.61; P<0.001). Major bleeding was 3.3% vs 1.8% (HR 1.87; 95% CI 0.90–3.89; P=0.09), i.e. not significantly higher, though gastrointestinal bleeding was substantially more frequent with edoxaban; all-cause death did not differ (9.9% vs 10.2%; HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.69–1.36).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"The annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolism was 2.3% in the edoxaban group and 6.7% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.19 to 0.61; P<0.001)"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"the annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.3% in the edoxaban group and 1.8% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.87; 95% CI, 0.90 to 3.89; P = 0.09)" -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"There were substantially more events of gastrointestinal bleeding in the edoxaban group than in the placebo group."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"There was no substantial between-group difference in death from any cause (9.9% in the edoxaban group and 10.2% in the placebo group; hazard ratio, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.36)."} -->

Taken together: against warfarin, low-dose regimens buy bleeding safety at some cost in ischaemic stroke prevention; the 15 mg dose in ELDERCARE-AF is a distinct, much lower dose tested only against placebo in patients excluded from standard-dose therapy.

- **ARISTOTLE (apixaban):** primary outcome 1.27%/yr vs 1.60%/yr with warfarin (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.66–0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.01 for superiority), and the authors concluded apixaban was superior to warfarin for preventing stroke or systemic embolism. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.66 to 0.95; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.01 for superiority" } --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"apixaban was superior to warfarin in preventing stroke or systemic embolism" } -->
- **RE-LY (dabigatran 150 mg):** 1.11%/yr vs 1.69%/yr with warfarin (RR 0.66; 95% CI 0.53–0.82; P<0.001 for superiority). The 110 mg dose met only non-inferiority (RR 0.91; 95% CI 0.74–1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"relative risk, 0.66; 95% CI, 0.53 to 0.82; P<0.001 for superiority" } --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"relative risk with dabigatran, 0.91; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 1.11; P<0.001 for noninferiority" } -->

**Non-inferior only**

- **ROCKET AF (rivaroxaban):** primary analysis HR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66–0.96; P<0.001 for noninferiority); in the intention-to-treat analysis HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.74–1.03; P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority). Conclusion: rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"P<0.001 for noninferiority; P=0.12 for superiority" } --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"rivaroxaban was noninferior to warfarin for the prevention of stroke or systemic embolism" } -->
- **ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban):** both regimens tested for non-inferiority; high-dose HR 0.79 (97.5% CI 0.63–0.99; P<0.001 for noninferiority), low-dose HR 1.07 (97.5% CI 0.87–1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority); in the intention-to-treat analysis the trend favouring high-dose edoxaban was not significant (HR 0.87; 97.5% CI 0.73–1.04; P=0.08). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"Both once-daily regimens of edoxaban were noninferior to warfarin with respect to the prevention of stroke or systemic embolism" } --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"hazard ratio, 0.87; 97.5% CI, 0.73 to 1.04; P=0.08" } -->

**Meta-analysis (RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48; 71,683 participants)**

- Stroke or systemic embolism reduced by 19% (RR 0·81, 95% CI 0·73–0·91; p<0·0001), mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38–0·64; p<0·0001) <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38-0·64; p<0·0001)"} -->
- All-cause mortality reduced (0·90, 0·85–0·95; p=0·0003) <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"New oral anticoagulants also significantly reduced all-cause mortality (0·90, 0·85-0·95; p=0·0003)"} -->
- Intracranial haemorrhage reduced (0·48, 0·39–0·59; p<0·0001) <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"and intracranial haemorrhage (0·48, 0·39-0·59; p<0·0001), but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1·25, 1·01-1·55; p=0·04)"} -->
- Gastrointestinal bleeding increased (1·25, 1·01–1·55; p=0·04) <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"but increased gastrointestinal bleeding (1·25, 1·01-1·55; p=0·04)"} -->
- Conditions: the major-bleeding benefit was greater where centre-based time in therapeutic range was <66% (0·69, 0·59–0·81 vs 0·93, 0·76–1·13; p for interaction 0·022); low-dose regimens showed similar stroke/SEE reductions (1·03, 0·84–1·27; p=0·74) but more ischaemic strokes (1·28, 1·02–1·60; p=0·045).

**Consistency with the individual trials — yes, directionally**

- RE-LY: haemorrhagic stroke 0.38%/yr with warfarin vs 0.12%/yr with dabigatran 110 mg and 0.10%/yr with 150 mg (both P<0.001) — a reduction of roughly 70–75%, consistent with the pooled RR 0·49 <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.38% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 0.12% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001)."} -->
- ARISTOTLE: haemorrhagic stroke 0.24%/yr vs 0.47%/yr (HR 0.51, 95% CI 0.35–0.75; P<0.001) — essentially identical to the pooled estimate <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.24% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 0.47% per year in the warfarin group (hazard ratio, 0.51; 95% CI, 0.35 to 0.75; P<0.001)"} -->

So both trials individually reported a roughly halving or greater of haemorrhagic stroke versus warfarin, matching the meta-analysis's pooled 51% relative reduction. Note the meta-analysis pools all four trials and both dabigatran doses, so its point estimate is not a dose-specific comparison.

**RE-LY (dabigatran, "Dabigatran versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation")**
- Major bleeding: warfarin 3.36%/yr vs dabigatran 110 mg 2.71%/yr (P=0.003) and 150 mg 3.11%/yr (P=0.31, not significant). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 3.36% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 2.71% per year in the group receiving 110 mg of dabigatran (P=0.003) and 3.11% per year in the group receiving 150 mg of dabigatran (P=0.31)."} -->
- Condition: 18,113 patients with AF and stroke risk; blinded fixed dabigatran doses vs unblinded adjusted-dose warfarin; median follow-up 2.0 years. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"we randomly assigned 18,113 patients who had atrial fibrillation and a risk of stroke to receive, in a blinded fashion, fixed doses of dabigatran--110 mg or 150 mg twice daily--or, in an unblinded fashion, adjusted-dose warfarin"} -->

**ROCKET AF (rivaroxaban, "Rivaroxaban versus warfarin in nonvalvular atrial fibrillation")**
- The paper reports the composite of major and clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding, not major bleeding alone: 14.9%/yr with rivaroxaban vs 14.5%/yr with warfarin (HR 1.03; 95% CI 0.96–1.11; P=0.44), with lower intracranial (0.5% vs 0.7%, P=0.02) and fatal bleeding (0.2% vs 0.5%, P=0.003). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"Major and nonmajor clinically relevant bleeding occurred in 1475 patients in the rivaroxaban group (14.9% per year) and in 1449 in the warfarin group (14.5% per year) (hazard ratio, 1.03; 95% CI, 0.96 to 1.11; P=0.44)"} -->
- The conclusions state no significant between-group difference in major bleeding. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"There was no significant between-group difference in the risk of major bleeding, although intracranial and fatal bleeding occurred less frequently in the rivaroxaban group."} -->
- Condition: 14,264 patients with nonvalvular AF at increased stroke risk; rivaroxaban 20 mg daily vs dose-adjusted warfarin, double-blind; per-protocol as-treated primary analysis. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8ff4bad2e9d926335b4de77ad1e41630","quote":"we randomly assigned 14,264 patients with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation who were at increased risk for stroke to receive either rivaroxaban (at a daily dose of 20 mg) or dose-adjusted warfarin"} -->

**ARISTOTLE (apixaban, "Apixaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation")**
- Major bleeding: 2.13%/yr with apixaban vs 3.09%/yr with warfarin (HR 0.69; 95% CI 0.60–0.80; P<0.001). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"The rate of major bleeding was 2.13% per year in the apixaban group, as compared with 3.09% per year in the warfarin group (hazard ratio, 0.69; 95% CI, 0.60 to 0.80; P<0.001)"} -->
- Condition: 18,201 patients with AF plus ≥1 additional stroke risk factor; apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs warfarin (target INR 2.0–3.0), double-blind; median follow-up 1.8 years. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_81e343c146c92d15d7c2f15b65748ce1","quote":"we compared apixaban (at a dose of 5 mg twice daily) with warfarin (target international normalized ratio, 2.0 to 3.0) in 18,201 patients with atrial fibrillation and at least one additional risk factor for stroke"} -->

**ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban, "Edoxaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation")**
- Major bleeding: 3.43%/yr with warfarin vs 2.75%/yr with high-dose edoxaban (HR 0.80; 95% CI 0.71–0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61%/yr with low-dose edoxaban (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"The annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.43% with warfarin versus 2.75% with high-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.80; 95% CI, 0.71 to 0.91; P<0.001) and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)."} -->
- Condition: 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk AF; two once-daily edoxaban regimens vs warfarin, double-blind double-dummy; median follow-up 2.8 years; major bleeding was the principal safety end point. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years)"} -->

Note: the ROCKET AF source does not give a standalone major-bleeding rate for rivaroxaban versus warfarin; only the composite figure and the conclusion of no significant difference are stated.

**ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48 (edoxaban vs warfarin, median TTR 68.4%)** — low-dose (30 mg) edoxaban was noninferior to warfarin for stroke/systemic embolism, but with no efficacy advantage and a strong reduction in major bleeding. During treatment, the annualized primary event rate was 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% with warfarin (HR 1.07; 97.5% CI 0.87–1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority), and in the intention-to-treat analysis there was an unfavorable trend (HR 1.13; 97.5% CI 0.96–1.34; P=0.10). Major bleeding was 1.61% vs 3.43% (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001). Both regimens were noninferior with significantly lower bleeding and cardiovascular death.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 1.07; 97.5% confidence interval [CI], 0.87 to 1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and an unfavorable trend with low-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 1.13; 97.5% CI, 0.96 to 1.34; P=0.10)" -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)."} -->

**Meta-analysis of the four pivotal trials (RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48; 71,683 participants)** — pooled low-dose NOAC regimens gave stroke/systemic embolic event reductions similar to warfarin (RR 1.03; 0.84–1.27; p=0.74) and a more favorable bleeding profile (0.65; 0.43–1.00; p=0.05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1.28; 1.02–1.60; p=0.045). Separately, the relative reduction in major bleeding was greater where centre-based TTR was <66% than ≥66% (0.69, 0.59–0.81 vs 0.93, 0.76–1.13; p for interaction 0.022).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"Low-dose new oral anticoagulant regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (1·03, 0·84-1·27; p=0·74), and a more favourable bleeding profile (0·65, 0·43-1·00; p=0·05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1·28, 1·02-1·60; p=0·045)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"there was a greater relative reduction in major bleeding with new oral anticoagulants when the centre-based time in therapeutic range was less than 66% than when it was 66% or more (0·69, 0·59-0·81 vs 0·93, 0·76-1·13; p for interaction 0·022)"} -->

**ELDERCARE-AF (15 mg edoxaban vs placebo)** — in Japanese patients ≥80 years with nonvalvular AF judged unsuitable for approved-dose anticoagulation (984 randomized, 492 per arm), edoxaban was superior to placebo for stroke/systemic embolism: annualized 2.3% vs 6.7% (HR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19–0.61; P<0.001). Major bleeding was 3.3% vs 1.8% (HR 1.87; 95% CI 0.90–3.89; P=0.09), i.e. not significantly higher, though gastrointestinal bleeding was substantially more frequent with edoxaban; all-cause death did not differ (9.9% vs 10.2%; HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.69–1.36).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"The annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolism was 2.3% in the edoxaban group and 6.7% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.34; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.19 to 0.61; P<0.001)"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"the annualized rate of major bleeding was 3.3% in the edoxaban group and 1.8% in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.87; 95% CI, 0.90 to 3.89; P = 0.09)" -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"There were substantially more events of gastrointestinal bleeding in the edoxaban group than in the placebo group."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"There was no substantial between-group difference in death from any cause (9.9% in the edoxaban group and 10.2% in the placebo group; hazard ratio, 0.97; 95% CI, 0.69 to 1.36)."} -->

Taken together: against warfarin, low-dose regimens buy bleeding safety at some cost in ischaemic stroke prevention; the 15 mg dose in ELDERCARE-AF is a distinct, much lower dose tested only against placebo in patients excluded from standard-dose therapy.

Taken together: low-dose regimens buy bleeding safety at the cost of some ischaemic-stroke efficacy against warfarin, whereas in very elderly patients unsuitable for standard doses, 15 mg edoxaban is clearly better than no anticoagulation.

**AVERROES** (apixaban 5 mg twice daily vs aspirin 81–324 mg/day; 5,599 patients with AF at increased stroke risk for whom vitamin K antagonist therapy was unsuitable): stroke or systemic embolism occurred in 51 patients (1.6%/year) on apixaban vs 113 (3.7%/year) on aspirin (HR 0.45; 95% CI 0.32–0.62; P<0.001), with no significant increase in major bleeding or intracranial hemorrhage; first cardiovascular hospitalization 12.6% vs 15.9%/year.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405","quote":"There were 51 primary outcome events (1.6% per year) among patients assigned to apixaban and 113 (3.7% per year) among those assigned to aspirin (hazard ratio with apixaban, 0.45; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.32 to 0.62; P<0.001)."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_ee77d1914d18a5ece9857b4e40a81405","quote":"apixaban reduced the risk of stroke or systemic embolism without significantly increasing the risk of major bleeding or intracranial hemorrhage"} -->

**ELDERCARE-AF** (edoxaban 15 mg once daily vs placebo; 984 Japanese patients ≥80 years with nonvalvular AF not appropriate candidates for standard anticoagulant doses): edoxaban was superior to placebo for stroke or systemic embolism and did not significantly increase major bleeding (ISTH definition); all-cause death 9.9% vs 10.2% (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.69–1.36).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_0e9d75e95b4aa172897de8e3f4333228","quote":"a once-daily 15-mg dose of edoxaban was superior to placebo in preventing stroke or systemic embolism and did not result in a significantly higher incidence of major bleeding than placebo"} -->

**ELDERCARE-AF (15 mg edoxaban vs placebo, Japanese patients ≥80 years ineligible for standard doses, n=984):** annualized stroke or systemic embolism 2.3% vs 6.7% (HR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19–0.61; P<0.001); major bleeding 3.3% vs 1.8% (HR 1.87; 95% CI 0.90–3.89; P=0.09), not significantly higher, though with substantially more gastrointestinal bleeding; all-cause death 9.9% vs 10.2% (HR 0.97; 95% CI 0.69–1.36). - **Haemorrhagic stroke:** RR 0·49 (0·38–0·64; p<0·0001).
- **All-cause mortality:** RR 0·90 (0·85–0·95; p=0·0003).
- **Intracranial haemorrhage:** RR 0·48 (0·39–0·59; p<0·0001).

answer:
**Short answer: only in DAPA-HF was cardiovascular death significantly reduced on its own. In DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved the benefit was driven by heart failure events, with CV death not reaching significance; the meta-analysis found a borderline CV-death effect in preserved EF and a modest but significant one across all five trials.**

**DAPA-HF (EF ≤40%, n=4744):** CV death occurred in 227 (9.6%) vs 273 (11.5%), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98); all-cause death 11.6% vs 13.9%, HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97). The primary outcome was the composite of worsening HF or CV death.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**DELIVER (EF >40%, n=6263):** primary composite 16.4% vs 19.5%, HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92); worsening HF HR 0.79 (0.69–0.91); CV death 7.4% vs 8.3%, HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05) — not significant.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved (EF >40%, n=5988):** primary composite 13.8% vs 17.1%, HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), and the effect was explicitly attributed to fewer HF hospitalizations rather than to CV death.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group."} -->

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** in DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved (12,251 participants) the composite fell to HR 0.80 (0.73–0.87), with CV death 0.88 (0.77–1.00) — the upper bound touching 1 — and first HF hospitalization 0.74 (0.67–0.83). Across all five trials, CV death was 0.87 (0.79–0.95), first HF hospitalization 0.72 (0.67–0.78), all-cause mortality 0.92 (0.86–0.99), composite 0.77 (0.72–0.82).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82]), cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95])"} -->

So the mortality benefit is clearest in reduced EF; in preserved EF the mortality reduction is small and not individually significant, while the reduction in HF hospitalization is robust in both.

In ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48, 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation were randomized (median follow-up 2.8 years). In the warfarin group, the median time in the therapeutic range was 68.4%, in the on-treatment analysis of the primary efficacy end point. Both figures come from the trial report "Edoxaban versus warfarin in patients with atrial fibrillation" (NEJM 2013).

<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"comparing two once-daily regimens of edoxaban with warfarin in 21,105 patients with moderate-to-high-risk atrial fibrillation (median follow-up, 2.8 years)"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"The annualized rate of the primary end point during treatment was 1.50% with warfarin (median time in the therapeutic range, 68.4%)"} -->

**Short answer: the reduction in cardiovascular death on its own was small and not statistically significant in the two preserved-EF trials; it was significant only in DAPA-HF, and in the meta-analysis only once the reduced-EF trials were pooled in.**

**DAPA-HF** (reduced EF ≤40%): CV death 227/2373 (9.6%) vs 273/2371 (11.5%), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98) — a nominally significant standalone CV-mortality benefit; all-cause death HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97).<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**DELIVER** (EF >40%): CV death 231 (7.4%) vs 261 (8.3%), HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05) — not significant; the benefit came from worsening HF, HR 0.79 (0.69–0.91).<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved** (EF >40%): primary composite HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), but "this effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure"; total HF hospitalizations HR 0.73 (0.61–0.88).<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group."} --> The abstract gives no separate CV-death estimate for this trial.

**Meta-analysis** (five trials, 21,947 participants): in DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved alone (n=12,251), CV death HR 0.88 (0.77–1.00) — the upper confidence limit touches 1, so not significant on its own; HF hospitalization HR 0.74 (0.67–0.83).<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"with consistent reductions in both components: cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} --> Across all five trials, CV death became significant at HR 0.87 (0.79–0.95), along with all-cause mortality 0.92 (0.86–0.99).<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95]), first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·72 [0·67-0·78]), and all-cause mortality (0·92 [0·86-0·99])"} -->

**Primary composite outcome in each trial**

- **DAPA-HF** (EF ≤40%; primary outcome: worsening HF or CV death): 16.3% vs 21.2%, HR 0.74 (95% CI 0.65–0.85), P<0.001, over a median of 18.2 months — *Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"the primary outcome occurred in 386 of 2373 patients (16.3%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 502 of 2371 patients (21.2%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.74; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.85; P<0.001)"} -->
- **EMPEROR-Reduced** (EF ≤40%; CV death or HF hospitalization): 19.4% vs 24.7%, HR 0.75 (0.65–0.86), P<0.001, median 16 months — *Cardiovascular and Renal Outcomes with Empagliflozin in Heart Failure*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"a primary outcome event occurred in 361 of 1863 patients (19.4%) in the empagliflozin group and in 462 of 1867 patients (24.7%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio for cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001)"} -->
- **EMPEROR-Preserved** (EF >40%; CV death or HF hospitalization): 13.8% vs 17.1%, HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), P<0.001, median 26.2 months; effect mainly driven by fewer HF hospitalizations — *Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"a primary outcome event occurred in 415 of 2997 patients (13.8%) in the empagliflozin group and in 511 of 2991 patients (17.1%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.79; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.69 to 0.90; P<0.001)"} -->
- **DELIVER** (EF >40%; worsening HF or CV death): 16.4% vs 19.5%, HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92), P<0.001, median 2.3 years — *Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"the primary outcome occurred in 512 of 3131 patients (16.4%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 610 of 3132 patients (19.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.73 to 0.92; P<0.001)"} -->

**Across the ejection fraction range**

- The effect appears consistent: in the prespecified meta-analysis of the five trials, the composite of CV death or HF hospitalization was reduced with HR 0.77 (0.72–0.82) across 21,947 participants, and treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction — *SGLT-2 inhibitors in patients with heart failure: a comprehensive meta-analysis of five randomised controlled trials*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"Treatment effects on the primary endpoint were generally consistent across the 14 subgroups examined, including ejection fraction."} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82])"} -->
- Within DELIVER, results were similar in patients with EF ≥60% and those with EF <60% — *Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction*. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"Results were similar among patients with a left ventricular ejection fraction of 60% or more and those with a left ventricular ejection fraction of less than 60%"} -->
- Caveat: the magnitude is somewhat smaller in the higher-EF trials (0.79–0.82) than in the reduced-EF trials (0.74–0.75), and in the higher-EF trials the benefit is driven mainly by HF hospitalization, with CV death not significantly reduced in DELIVER (HR 0.88, 0.74–1.05). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

Yes for DAPA-HF only; the other trials and the meta-analysis did not show a significant stand-alone reduction in cardiovascular death.

- **DAPA-HF** (reduced EF ≤40%): death from cardiovascular causes fell significantly — 227/2373 (9.6%) vs 273/2371 (11.5%), HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98), over a median 18.2 months. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->
- **DELIVER** (EF >40%): the benefit was reported only as a composite — dapagliflozin reduced the combined risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death; no separate cardiovascular-death result is given. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"Dapagliflozin reduced the combined risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death among patients with heart failure and a mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction."} -->
- **EMPEROR-Preserved** (EF >40%): the primary composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure fell (HR 0.79; 95% CI 0.69–0.90), but this was mainly due to fewer heart failure hospitalizations — i.e. no stand-alone cardiovascular-death effect. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group."} -->
- **Meta-analysis of five trials**: across DELIVER and EMPEROR-Preserved (12,251 participants), cardiovascular death alone was HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.77–1.00) — not significant, at the boundary — while first hospitalization for heart failure was 0.74 (0.67–0.83). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"with consistent reductions in both components: cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->

So the reduction in cardiovascular death on its own is demonstrated only in the reduced-ejection-fraction DAPA-HF trial; in the preserved/mildly reduced EF trials and in the meta-analysis the driven component is heart failure hospitalization. The knowledge base does not give a separate cardiovascular-death hazard ratio for DELIVER or for the pooled five-trial population.

**Entry criteria differed mainly in albuminuria and diabetes:**

answer:
**Short answer: only in DAPA-HF. In both HFmrEF/HFpEF trials the benefit was driven by heart-failure events, not CV death; the meta-analysis found a modest CV-death reduction that was borderline in the preserved-EF pair but significant across all five trials.**

**DAPA-HF (HFrEF, EF ≤40%, n=4744):** CV death was significantly reduced on its own — 9.6% vs 11.5%, HR 0.82 (95% CI 0.69–0.98); all-cause death 11.6% vs 13.9%, HR 0.83 (0.71–0.97).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"Death from cardiovascular causes occurred in 227 patients (9.6%) in the dapagliflozin group and in 273 patients (11.5%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.82; 95% CI, 0.69 to 0.98)"} -->

**DELIVER (EF >40%, n=6263):** primary composite HR 0.82 (0.73–0.92), driven by worsening HF (HR 0.79, 0.69–0.91); CV death alone was not significant — 7.4% vs 8.3%, HR 0.88 (0.74–1.05).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"cardiovascular death occurred in 231 patients (7.4%) and 261 patients (8.3%), respectively (hazard ratio, 0.88; 95% CI, 0.74 to 1.05)"} -->

**EMPEROR-Preserved (EF >40%, n=5998):** primary composite HR 0.79 (0.69–0.90), but explicitly driven by HF hospitalization, with no separate CV-death benefit reported.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"This effect was mainly related to a lower risk of hospitalization for heart failure in the empagliflozin group."} -->

**Meta-analysis (five trials, 21,947 participants):** in DELIVER + EMPEROR-Preserved (n=12,251), CV death HR 0·88 (0·77–1·00) — confidence limit touching 1 — versus HF hospitalization 0·74 (0·67–0·83).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"with consistent reductions in both components: cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00]) and first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·74 [0·67-0·83])"} -->

Across all five trials, CV death was significantly reduced: 0·87 (0·79–0·95), with all-cause mortality 0·92 (0·86–0·99) and HF hospitalization 0·72 (0·67–0·78).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"SGLT2 inhibitors reduced the risk of composite cardiovascular death or hospitalisation for heart failure (0·77 [0·72-0·82]), cardiovascular death (0·87 [0·79-0·95]), first hospitalisation for heart failure (0·72 [0·67-0·78]), and all-cause mortality (0·92 [0·86-0·99])"} -->

So the CV-death effect is clearest in HFrEF; at higher ejection fractions the mortality signal is weaker and the composite benefit is carried mainly by reduced HF hospitalization.

**No significant difference:** The knowledge base does not contain all-cause mortality results for any individual SGLT2 inhibitor trial (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced, EMPEROR-Preserved, DELIVER, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY, CREDENCE); the available records for these trials do not report all-cause death. So no individual SGLT2 trial can be identified here as having found no significant difference in death from any cause.

**Heart failure trials**

- DAPA-HF: adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction and hypoglycemia did not differ between dapagliflozin and placebo. (Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction)

- EMPEROR-Preserved: uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin. (Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction)
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin."} -->

**Chronic kidney disease trials**

- EMPA-KIDNEY: rates of serious adverse events were similar between empagliflozin and placebo. (Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease)

<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"There were no significant differences in rates of amputation or fracture."} -->

answer: The knowledge base's SGLT2-inhibitor documents (DAPA-HF, EMPEROR-Reduced, EMPEROR-Preserved, DELIVER, DAPA-CKD, EMPA-KIDNEY, CREDENCE, and the five-trial meta-analysis) contain only background, methods, results and conclusions lines. None of them reports adverse events, safety outcomes, or "no difference from placebo" findings: the word "adverse" appears only in background sentences about risk of adverse kidney and cardiovascular outcomes, and searches for safety results found nothing. So the knowledge base does not say what adverse events or safety signals these trials reported, and does not say where they found no difference from placebo.

In DAPA-CKD (Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease), the number needed to treat to prevent one primary outcome event was **19 (95% CI, 15 to 27)**.

This applies to the primary composite outcome (sustained decline in eGFR of at least 50%, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes), over a median follow-up of 2.4 years, with 9.2% vs 14.5% events (dapagliflozin vs placebo; HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.51 to 0.72). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"number needed to treat to prevent one primary outcome event, 19 [95% CI, 15 to 27]"} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"Over a median of 2.4 years, a primary outcome event occurred in 197 of 2152 participants (9.2%) in the dapagliflozin group and 312 of 2152 participants (14.5%) in the placebo group"} -->

**Heart failure trials — adverse events reported:**

- In DAPA-HF (dapagliflozin, reduced ejection fraction), adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups — i.e., no excess of these events versus placebo. In Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction: "The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups."} -->
- In EMPEROR-Preserved (empagliflozin, preserved ejection fraction), uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin. In Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction: "Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin."} -->
- In EMPEROR-Reduced (empagliflozin, reduced ejection fraction), uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin. In Cardiovascular and Renal Outcomes with Empagliflozin in Heart Failure: "Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin."} -->

**Chronic kidney disease trials:**

- In EMPA-KIDNEY (empagliflozin; eGFR and albuminuria-based CKD population), the rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups. In Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease: "The rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"The rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups."} -->
- In DAPA-CKD (dapagliflozin; eGFR 25–75 and UACR 200–5000), the known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed, with effects similar in participants with and without type 2 diabetes. In Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease: "The known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed."} -->

**Where no difference from placebo was found:** volume depletion, renal dysfunction and hypoglycemia events (DAPA-HF); overall serious adverse events (EMPA-KIDNEY). EMPA-KIDNEY also found no significant between-group difference for hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death (4.0% vs 4.6%) or all-cause death (4.5% vs 5.1%) — though those are efficacy outcomes, not safety events. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"there were no significant between-group differences with respect to the composite outcome of hospitalization for heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes"} -->

The knowledge base does not give adverse-event data for DELIVER or SOLOIST-WHF.

answer:
**Populations**

- **CREDENCE** (canagliflozin): all patients had type 2 diabetes and albuminuric CKD, with eGFR 30 to <90 ml/min/1.73 m² and albuminuria (ACR >300 to 5000 mg/g), all on RAS blockade. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"All the patients had an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 30 to <90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and albuminuria (ratio of albumin [mg] to creatinine [g], >300 to 5000) and were treated with renin-angiotensin system blockade."} -->
- **DAPA-CKD** (dapagliflozin): 4304 participants with eGFR 25 to 75 ml/min/1.73 m² and ACR 200 to 5000 mg/g — i.e., albuminuric CKD, enrolled with or without type 2 diabetes. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"We randomly assigned 4304 participants with an estimated glomerular filtration rate (GFR) of 25 to 75 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area and a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of 200 to 5000"} -->
- **EMPA-KIDNEY** (empagliflozin): broader entry — eGFR ≥20 to <45 ml/min/1.73 m², **or** eGFR ≥45 to <90 with ACR ≥200 mg/g, so it included patients with lower eGFR and/or lesser albuminuria than the other two. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 20 but less than 45 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area, or who had an eGFR of at least 45 but less than 90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of at least 200"} -->

**Consistency with and without diabetes**

- DAPA-CKD: effects were similar in participants with and without type 2 diabetes, and the primary composite (≥50% eGFR decline, ESKD, or renal/CV death) was significantly reduced regardless of diabetes status (HR 0.61; 95% CI 0.51–0.72). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The effects of dapagliflozin were similar in participants with type 2 diabetes and in those without type 2 diabetes."} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"the risk of a composite of a sustained decline in the estimated GFR of at least 50%, end-stage kidney disease, or death from renal or cardiovascular causes was significantly lower with dapagliflozin than with placebo"} -->
- EMPA-KIDNEY: results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across eGFR subgroups. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"Results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across subgroups defined according to eGFR ranges."} -->
- CREDENCE: enrolled only patients with type 2 diabetes, so it provides no diabetes-independent comparison; kidney failure and CV events were lower with canagliflozin at a median 2.62 years. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"In patients with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease, the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events was lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group at a median follow-up of 2.62 years."} -->

- **EMPA-KIDNEY** (empagliflozin): broader entry — eGFR ≥20 to <45 ml/min/1.73 m², **or** eGFR ≥45 to <90 with ACR ≥200 mg/g, so it included patients with lower eGFR and/or lesser albuminuria than the other two. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) of at least 20 but less than 45 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 of body-surface area, or who had an eGFR of at least 45 but less than 90 ml per minute per 1.73 m2 with a urinary albumin-to-creatinine ratio (with albumin measured in milligrams and creatinine measured in grams) of at least 200"} -->

- EMPA-KIDNEY: results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across eGFR subgroups. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"Results were consistent among patients with or without diabetes and across subgroups defined according to eGFR ranges."} -->
- CREDENCE: enrolled only patients with type 2 diabetes, so it provides no diabetes-independent comparison; kidney failure and CV events were lower with canagliflozin at a median 2.62 years. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"In patients with type 2 diabetes and kidney disease, the risk of kidney failure and cardiovascular events was lower in the canagliflozin group than in the placebo group at a median follow-up of 2.62 years."} -->

- CREDENCE: type 2 diabetes was required in all patients. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"we assigned patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease"} -->
- DAPA-CKD: enrolled with or without type 2 diabetes. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The effect of dapagliflozin in patients with chronic kidney disease, with or without type 2 diabetes, is not known." -->

answer:
No SGLT2 inhibitor trial or analysis in the knowledge base reports a reduction in death from any cause, and none reports a non-significant all-cause mortality result either — the documents record only cardiovascular death, and even that not as a standalone all-cause finding.

What the SGLT2 documents do say:

- DAPA-HF (dapagliflozin, HFrEF): the benefit was on the composite of worsening heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes (HR 0.74; 95% CI 0.65–0.85) — "the risk of worsening heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes was lower among those who received dapagliflozin." <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"the risk of worsening heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes was lower among those who received dapagliflozin than among those who received placebo"}} -->
- EMPEROR-Reduced (empagliflozin, HFrEF): lower risk of the composite of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure (HR 0.75; 95% CI 0.65–0.86). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"those in the empagliflozin group had a lower risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure than those in the placebo group"}} -->
- EMPEROR-Preserved and DELIVER: reduced combined risk of cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization/worsening heart failure in HFmrEF/HFpEF. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"Empagliflozin reduced the combined risk of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure in patients with heart failure and a preserved ejection fraction"}} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"Dapagliflozin reduced the combined risk of worsening heart failure or cardiovascular death among patients with heart failure with a mildly reduced or preserved ejection fraction"}} -->
- The five-trial meta-analysis: cardiovascular death HR 0.88 (95% CI 0.77–1.00) — the upper bound reaching 1.00, i.e. not a clear significant reduction even for cardiovascular death. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4b1be72f0031135f81e0915e571e919b","quote":"cardiovascular death (0·88 [0·77-1·00])"}} -->
- The chronic kidney disease trials (dapagliflozin, empagliflozin) and CREDENCE (canagliflozin) are described by their kidney and cardiovascular composite outcomes; the knowledge base does not state any all-cause mortality result for them.

The only all-cause mortality findings present come from aspirin trials (ASPREE: higher all-cause mortality with aspirin, HR 1.14), which are not SGLT2 studies. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_400696c0380783b1753ade39d010ccba","quote":"The risk of death from any cause was 12.7 events per 1000 person-years in the aspirin group and 11.1 events per 1000 person-years in the placebo group"}} -->

In CREDENCE, patients received canagliflozin 100 mg once daily (or placebo), in a double-blind randomized trial of patients with type 2 diabetes and albuminuric chronic kidney disease (eGFR 30 to <90 ml/min/1.73 m², albumin-to-creatinine ratio >300 to 5000 mg/g, all on renin–angiotensin system blockade). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"to receive canagliflozin, an oral SGLT2 inhibitor, at a dose of 100 mg daily or placebo"} -->

The trial was stopped early after a planned interim analysis on the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring committee; at that time 4401 patients had undergone randomization and median follow-up was 2.62 years. <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"The trial was stopped early after a planned interim analysis on the recommendation of the data and safety monitoring committee. At that time, 4401 patients had undergone randomization, with a median follow-up of 2.62 years." -->

- **ARRIVE** (moderate estimated risk, 100 mg enteric-coated aspirin vs placebo, 12,546 patients, median 60 months): the primary composite endpoint (cardiovascular death, MI, unstable angina, stroke or TIA) occurred in 269 (4.29%) on aspirin vs 281 (4.48%) on placebo — HR 0.96; 95% CI 0.81–1.13; p=0.6038, i.e. not significant. Gastrointestinal bleeding was higher with aspirin (0.97% vs 0.46%; HR 2.11). (ARRIVE, Lancet 2018)

- **ASCEND** (diabetes without evident cardiovascular disease, aspirin 100 mg daily, 15,480 participants, mean 7.4 years): serious vascular events were significantly lower with aspirin — 658 (8.5%) vs 743 (9.6%); rate ratio 0.88; 95% CI 0.79–0.97; P=0.01 — but major bleeding was higher (4.1% vs 3.2%; rate ratio 1.29; 95% CI 1.09–1.52; P=0.003), so the absolute benefits were largely counterbalanced by bleeding. (ASCEND, NEJM 2018)

- **ASPREE** (healthy older adults, low-dose aspirin, 19,114 participants, median 4.7 years): cardiovascular disease rate 10.7 vs 11.3 events per 1000 person-years — HR 0.95; 95% CI 0.83–1.08 — not significantly lower, while major hemorrhage was significantly higher (8.6 vs 6.2 per 1000 person-years; HR 1.38; 95% CI 1.18–1.62; P<0.001). **Heart failure trials**

- DAPA-HF (dapagliflozin, reduced EF): adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction and hypoglycemia did not differ from placebo — *Dapagliflozin in Patients with Heart Failure and Reduced Ejection Fraction* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_3d8122c20e1cbc078636f036dbe476b7","quote":"The frequency of adverse events related to volume depletion, renal dysfunction, and hypoglycemia did not differ between treatment groups."} -->
- EMPEROR-Reduced (empagliflozin): uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin — *Cardiovascular and Renal Outcomes with Empagliflozin in Heart Failure* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_b5b2f2860d0e0ed2b6663cb104221791","quote":"Uncomplicated genital tract infection was reported more frequently with empagliflozin."} -->
- EMPEROR-Preserved (empagliflozin, preserved EF): uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were more frequent with empagliflozin — *Empagliflozin in Heart Failure with a Preserved Ejection Fraction* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_343c67f35a2bf841907858fd63302653","quote":"Uncomplicated genital and urinary tract infections and hypotension were reported more frequently with empagliflozin."} -->
- DELIVER (dapagliflozin, mildly reduced/preserved EF): the incidence of adverse events was similar in the two groups — *Dapagliflozin in Heart Failure with Mildly Reduced or Preserved Ejection Fraction* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_e1fc1fa13a9a3fbf27de970c81e78bba","quote":"The incidence of adverse events was similar in the two groups."} -->

**Chronic kidney disease trials**

- DAPA-CKD: only that "the known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed"; no specific adverse-event rates are given in the document — *Dapagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_01c40038ab279aadbaf12401aadbad29","quote":"The known safety profile of dapagliflozin was confirmed."} -->
- EMPA-KIDNEY: rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups; no significant between-group difference in hospitalization for heart failure or cardiovascular death (4.0% vs 4.6%) or in death from any cause (4.5% vs 5.1%) — *Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"The rates of serious adverse events were similar in the two groups."} --> <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_9babb063478831150659a9e2e6b0e443","quote":"there were no significant between-group differences with respect to the composite outcome of hospitalization for heart failure or death from cardiovascular causes"} -->
- CREDENCE (canagliflozin, diabetic kidney disease): no significant differences in rates of amputation or fracture — *Canagliflozin and Renal Outcomes in Type 2 Diabetes and Nephropathy* <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_57ce472296b677f0d08707b04c50a8f0","quote":"There were no significant differences in rates of amputation or fracture."} -->

Source: "Empagliflozin in Patients with Chronic Kidney Disease."

answer:
**ARRIVE** (Lancet 2018): 12,546 patients at moderate estimated risk of a first cardiovascular event, enrolled at 501 sites in seven countries; eligible patients were men aged 55 or older and women aged 60 or older with average (moderate) cardiovascular risk based on risk-factor count, excluding those at high bleeding risk (including gastrointestinal bleeding) and those with diabetes. Aspirin 100 mg daily gave a primary endpoint rate of 4.29% vs 4.48% with placebo (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.81–1.13).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_a80cd40ea6db9ff8486b4ad6e10638d2","quote":"Eligible patients were aged 55 years (men) or 60 years (women) and older and had an average cardiovascular risk, deemed to be moderate on the basis of the number of specific risk factors. We excluded patients at high risk of gastrointestinal bleeding or other bleeding, or diabetes."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_a80cd40ea6db9ff8486b4ad6e10638d2","quote":"12 546 patients were enrolled and randomly assigned to receive aspirin (n=6270) or placebo (n=6276) at 501 study sites."} -->

**ASPREE** (NEJM 2018): community-dwelling persons in Australia and the United States aged 70 or older (65 or older among US blacks and Hispanics) without cardiovascular disease, dementia, or disability; 100 mg enteric-coated aspirin daily did not improve disability-free survival, with a numerically higher all-cause mortality.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_400696c0380783b1753ade39d010ccba","quote":"we enrolled community-dwelling persons in Australia and the United States who were 70 years of age or older (or ≥65 years of age among blacks and Hispanics in the United States) and did not have cardiovascular disease, dementia, or disability."} -->

**JPPP** (JAMA 2014): 14,464 Japanese patients aged 60–85 with hypertension, dyslipidemia, or diabetes, recruited by primary care physicians at 1007 clinics, followed up to 6.5 years; the 5-year primary outcome rate was 2.77% with aspirin vs 2.96% without (HR 0.94, 95% CI 0.77–1.15; P = .54).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8c085ce86e8550efe8d1ab710dba800f","quote":"Patients (N = 14,464) were aged 60 to 85 years, presenting with hypertension, dyslipidemia, or diabetes mellitus recruited by primary care physicians at 1007 clinics in Japan between March 2005 and June 2007"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8c085ce86e8550efe8d1ab710dba800f","quote":"hazard ratio [HR], 0.94 [95% CI, 0.77-1.15]; P = .54"} -->

**USPSTF** (recommendation statement): for adults 40–59 with 10% or greater 10-year CVD risk, the decision to start low-dose aspirin should be individual (C recommendation; small net benefit, moderate certainty); for adults 60 or older, it recommends against initiating low-dose aspirin (D recommendation; no net benefit, moderate certainty). The population addressed is adults 40 or older without signs/symptoms of CVD or known CVD and not at increased bleeding risk.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4634e2a7a07fd8375f49298d2fb101f7","quote":"The USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that aspirin use for the primary prevention of CVD events in adults aged 40 to 59 years who have a 10% or greater 10-year CVD risk has a small net benefit."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4634e2a7a07fd8375f49298d2fb101f7","quote":"The USPSTF recommends against initiating low-dose aspirin use for the primary prevention of CVD in adults 60 years or older. (D recommendation)."} -->

How the evidence relates: ARRIVE (men ≥55, women ≥60, moderate risk, no diabetes) and JPPP (Japanese, 60–85, with risk factors) both fell in the age band where the Task Force now permits individualized decisions, and both found no significant reduction in cardiovascular events — consistent with the "small net benefit" framing rather than a clear benefit. ASPREE (≥70, or ≥65 for US blacks and Hispanics, healthy older adults) falls squarely in the 60-or-older group for which the Task Force recommends against initiation, and its lack of benefit with numerically higher mortality supports that D recommendation. The knowledge base does not report any trial confined to adults aged 40–59, so the C recommendation for that band rests on the commissioned systematic review and modeling rather than on these three trials.

How the trials bear on this: none of the three enrolled adults aged 40–59, so they give no direct support to the C recommendation for that age band. **Benefit**

- 2009 (Lancet collaborative IPD meta-analysis, six primary-prevention trials, 95,000 participants): a 12% proportional reduction in serious vascular events (0.51% vs 0.57% per year, p=0.0001), driven mainly by roughly a fifth fewer non-fatal myocardial infarctions (0.18% vs 0.23% per year, p<0.0001); stroke effect not significant, vascular mortality unchanged (0.19% vs 0.19% per year, p=0.7).

<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"Vascular mortality did not differ significantly (0.19%vs 0.19% per year, p=0.7)."} -->

- 2009: increased major gastrointestinal and extracranial bleeds, 0.10% vs 0.07% per year (p<0.0001) — an absolute excess of about 0.03% per year, i.e. smaller than the 0.06% per year absolute reduction in serious vascular events.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"Aspirin allocation increased major gastrointestinal and extracranial bleeds (0.10%vs 0.07% per year, p<0.0001)"} -->
- 2019: major bleeding increased, HR 1.43 (1.30–1.56); 23.1 vs 16.4 per 10,000 participant-years; absolute risk increase 0.47% (0.34%–0.62%), NNH 210 — slightly larger than the 0.38% absolute cardiovascular reduction.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"(HR, 1.43 [95% credible interval, 1.30-1.56]; absolute risk increase, 0.47% [95% CI, 0.34%-0.62%]; number needed to harm, 210)"} -->

**Framing of net balance**

- 2009: "uncertain net value" — the reduction in occlusive events had to be weighed against any increase in major bleeds; further trials were awaited.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"aspirin is of uncertain net value as the reduction in occlusive events needs to be weighed against any increase in major bleeds"} -->
- 2019: a neutral, quantitative framing — lower cardiovascular risk and higher major bleeding risk, presented as information to inform patient discussions rather than a verdict either way; the harm (NNH 210) marginally outweighed the benefit (NNT 265).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"This information may inform discussions with patients about aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular events and bleeding."} -->

**Relation to the USPSTF recommendations** (adults ≥40 without CVD and not at increased bleeding risk)

- **Aged 40–59 with ≥10% 10-year CVD risk**: moderate certainty of a small net benefit; decision to start low-dose aspirin should be individual (C recommendation). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_4634e2a7a07fd8375f49298d2fb101f7","quote":"The USPSTF concludes with moderate certainty that aspirin use for the primary prevention of CVD events in adults aged 40 to 59 years who have a 10% or greater 10-year CVD risk has a small net benefit."} -->

(D recommendation)."} -->

How the trials bear on this: none of the three enrolled adults aged 40–59, so they give no direct support to the C recommendation for that age band. All three recruited populations aged 60 and over — ARRIVE (men ≥55, women ≥60), ASPREE (≥70, or ≥65 for black and Hispanic US participants) and JPPP (60–85) — and all found no significant reduction in cardiovascular events, with increased bleeding (ARRIVE: GI bleeding HR 2.11; ASPREE: major hemorrhage HR 1.38), consistent with the D recommendation against initiating aspirin at 60 or older. The documents do not state an explicit USPSTF appraisal of these individual trials.

In JPPP, the 5-year cumulative primary outcome event rate was 2.77% (95% CI 2.40%–3.20%) with aspirin versus 2.96% (95% CI 2.58%–3.40%) without aspirin, a non-significant difference (hazard ratio 0.94; 95% CI 0.77–1.15; P = .54) — in patients aged 60–85 years with hypertension, dyslipidemia, or diabetes (N = 14,464).

answer:
**Benefit**

- 2009 (Lancet collaborative IPD meta-analysis, six primary-prevention trials, 95,000 participants): a 12% proportional reduction in serious vascular events (0.51% vs 0.57% per year, p=0.0001), driven mainly by roughly a fifth fewer non-fatal myocardial infarctions (0.18% vs 0.23% per year, p<0.0001); stroke effect not significant, vascular mortality unchanged (0.19% vs 0.19% per year, p=0.7).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"In the primary prevention trials, aspirin allocation yielded a 12% proportional reduction in serious vascular events (0.51% aspirin vs 0.57% control per year, p=0.0001)"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"Vascular mortality did not differ significantly (0.19%vs 0.19% per year, p=0.7)."} -->
- 2019 (JAMA, 13 trials, 164,225 participants): composite of cardiovascular mortality, non-fatal MI and non-fatal stroke reduced, HR 0.89 (95% CrI 0.84–0.95); 57.1 vs 61.4 per 10,000 participant-years; absolute risk reduction 0.38% (0.20%–0.55%), NNT 265.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"(hazard ratio [HR], 0.89 [95% credible interval, 0.84-0.95]; absolute risk reduction, 0.38% [95% CI, 0.20%-0.55%]; number needed to treat, 265)"} -->

**Bleeding harm**

- 2009: increased major gastrointestinal and extracranial bleeds, 0.10% vs 0.07% per year (p<0.0001) — an absolute excess of about 0.03% per year, i.e. smaller than the 0.06% per year absolute reduction in serious vascular events.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"Aspirin allocation increased major gastrointestinal and extracranial bleeds (0.10%vs 0.07% per year, p<0.0001)"} -->
- 2019: major bleeding increased, HR 1.43 (1.30–1.56); 23.1 vs 16.4 per 10,000 participant-years; absolute risk increase 0.47% (0.34%–0.62%), NNH 210 — slightly larger than the 0.38% absolute cardiovascular reduction.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"(HR, 1.43 [95% credible interval, 1.30-1.56]; absolute risk increase, 0.47% [95% CI, 0.34%-0.62%]; number needed to harm, 210)"} -->

**Framing of net balance**

- 2009: "uncertain net value" — the reduction in occlusive events had to be weighed against any increase in major bleeds; further trials were awaited.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8d9ae273169bf27b347ca66421434090","quote":"aspirin is of uncertain net value as the reduction in occlusive events needs to be weighed against any increase in major bleeds"} -->
- 2019: a neutral, quantitative framing — lower cardiovascular risk and higher major bleeding risk, presented as information to inform patient discussions rather than a verdict either way; the harm (NNH 210) marginally outweighed the benefit (NNT 265).
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_64f23983bfe8fd167aa6725f288d7375","quote":"This information may inform discussions with patients about aspirin for primary prevention of cardiovascular events and bleeding."} -->

In short, the proportional benefit estimates are similar (12% relative vs HR 0.89), but the 2019 analysis quantifies the bleeding excess as larger in absolute terms than the cardiovascular gain, whereas the 2009 analysis reported a smaller absolute bleeding excess and left the balance explicitly open.

<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_400696c0380783b1753ade39d010ccba","quote":"The risk of death from any cause was 12.7 events per 1000 person-years in the aspirin group and 11.1 events per 1000 person-years in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 1.14; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.01 to 1.29)."} -->

**ASCEND** (diabetes without evident CVD, aspirin 100 mg/day vs placebo): no significant difference in gastrointestinal tract cancer (157 [2.0%] vs 158 [2.0%]) or all cancers (897 [11.6%] vs 887 [11.5%]); long-term follow-up for these outcomes was planned. The conclusion was that aspirin prevented serious vascular events but caused major bleeding, with absolute benefits largely counterbalanced by the bleeding hazard.
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_98e15daeb7feed7b008fd69ffce6745f","quote":"There was no significant difference between the aspirin group and the placebo group in the incidence of gastrointestinal tract cancer (157 participants [2.0%] and 158 [2.0%], respectively) or all cancers (897 [11.6%] and 887 [11.5%]); long-term follow-up for these outcomes is planned."} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_98e15daeb7feed7b008fd69ffce6745f","quote":"The absolute benefits were largely counterbalanced by the bleeding hazard."} -->

**ARRIVE** (moderate-risk primary-prevention population, aspirin 100 mg/day vs placebo): the knowledge base documents its design — primary efficacy endpoint was cardiovascular death, MI, unstable angina, stroke or TIA, with haemorrhagic events and other adverse events as safety endpoints — but it gives no all-cause mortality or cancer results for ARRIVE, so no comparison on those outcomes can be made from these sources.

- **All-cause mortality: RR 0.90 (0.85–0.95), p=0.0003** — significantly reduced.
- **Intracranial haemorrhage: RR 0.48 (0.39–0.59), p<0.0001** — significantly reduced.

**Consistency with the individual trials' own reports:**

- **RE-LY (dabigatran):** haemorrhagic stroke 0.38%/yr with warfarin vs 0.12%/yr with 110 mg (P<0.001) and 0.10%/yr with 150 mg (P<0.001) — i.e. relative reductions of roughly 68–74%, consistent in direction with the pooled 51% reduction.

- **ARISTOTLE (apixaban):** haemorrhagic stroke 0.24%/yr vs 0.47%/yr with warfarin, HR 0.51 (95% CI 0.35–0.75), P<0.001 — essentially identical to the pooled estimate of 0.49.

So yes: the meta-analysis's haemorrhagic-stroke finding is consistent with both trials individually — same direction and significance, with ARISTOTLE's hazard ratio (0.51) almost exactly matching the pooled RR (0.49) and RE-LY showing a somewhat larger reduction. - Haemorrhagic stroke: reduced by about half vs warfarin — RR 0.49 (95% CI 0.38–0.64; p<0.0001), and this mainly drove the 19% reduction in stroke or systemic embolism (RR 0.81, 0.73–0.91). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_68f0cec57cbc9a18bfbd4cfce07d3b63","quote":"mainly driven by a reduction in haemorrhagic stroke (0·49, 0·38-0·64; p<0·0001)"} -->

- Condition noted: the greater relative reduction in major bleeding with DOACs applied when centre-based TTR was <66% (RR 0.69, 0.59–0.81) rather than ≥66% (0.93, 0.76–1.13; p for interaction 0.022); low-dose regimens gave similar stroke/embolism reductions (1.03, 0.84–1.27) with more ischaemic strokes (1.28, 1.02–1.60; p=0.045).

**Consistency with the individual trials**

- RE-LY (dabigatran): consistent — haemorrhagic stroke 0.38%/yr with warfarin vs 0.12%/yr with 110 mg (P<0.001) and 0.10%/yr with 150 mg (P<0.001). <!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_8a669b066c4cb002e5224ef48c9a8550","quote":"The rate of hemorrhagic stroke was 0.38% per year in the warfarin group, as compared with 0.12% per year with 110 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001) and 0.10% per year with 150 mg of dabigatran (P<0.001)."} -->

- Both point the same way as the pooled RR of 0.49, so the meta-analysis' haemorrhagic stroke conclusion is consistent with the two trials' own reports.

**Low-dose edoxaban in ENGAGE AF-TIMI 48** (21,105 patients, median follow-up 2.8 years): during treatment, the annualized rate of stroke or systemic embolism was 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban vs 1.50% with warfarin (HR 1.07; 97.5% CI 0.87–1.31; P=0.005 for noninferiority) — so noninferiority was met, but with no efficacy advantage. In the intention-to-treat analysis there was an unfavorable trend (HR 1.13; 97.5% CI 0.96–1.34; P=0.10). Major bleeding was 1.61% vs 3.43% (HR 0.47; 95% CI 0.41–0.55; P<0.001), cardiovascular death 2.71% vs 3.17% (HR 0.85; 0.76–0.96; P=0.008), and the composite of stroke, systemic embolism or CV death 4.23% vs 4.43% (HR 0.95; 0.86–1.05; P=0.32).

<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and an unfavorable trend with low-dose edoxaban versus warfarin (hazard ratio, 1.13; 97.5% CI, 0.96 to 1.34; P=0.10)"} -->
<!-- evimed-source:{"sourceId":"src_1bcbd58b429315ec591b7e167517461a","quote":"and 1.61% with low-dose edoxaban (hazard ratio, 0.47; 95% CI, 0.41 to 0.55; P<0.001)"} -->

**Pooled low-dose regimens in the meta-analysis of the four pivotal trials**: low-dose NOAC regimens showed similar overall reductions in stroke or systemic embolic events to warfarin (RR 1.03, 95% CI 0.84–1.27; p=0.74) and a more favourable bleeding profile (0.65, 0.43–1.00; p=0.05), but significantly more ischaemic strokes (1.28, 1.02–1.60; p=0.045).

**15 mg edoxaban in ELDERCARE-AF** (984 Japanese patients ≥80 years, not appropriate candidates for standard-dose anticoagulation; 492 vs 492, placebo-controlled): annualized stroke or systemic embolism 2.3% vs 6.7% (HR 0.34; 95% CI 0.19–0.61; P<0.001); major bleeding 3.3% vs 1.8% (HR 1.87; 0.90–3.89; P=0.09), not significantly higher, though gastrointestinal bleeding events were substantially more frequent with edoxaban; all-cause death 9.9% vs 10.2% (HR 0.97; 0.69–1.36).

**Superiority on stroke or systemic embolism:**

- **RE-LY** (dabigatran): superiority was shown only for the 150 mg dose — 1.11%/yr vs 1.69%/yr with warfarin, RR 0.66 (95% CI 0.53–0.82), P<0.001 for superiority.
